items.title: William Ballariel Interview, 1959-10-02
items.q: And this fellow Johnny Post's father was leader then.

ctx.x: Well did you have that music in New Orleans? The Catholic Church didn't let them have a band on the street for the funeral. Did they do that here?

Yeah, they didn't have the band on the street. For the Catholic funeral? Yeah, if the Catholics wanted it, but they never did go in the church. Yes, I understand. Now my father was Catholic and the Excelsior Band played at his funeral when I was a little boy, you see. And that's when I remember a young Excelsior Band good. And this fellow Johnny Post's father was leader then. And my father was dead, oh my goodness, he's been dead. Just to think I'm about 70 years, because my next boyfriend will be in 70. He died…

Had your father played any music? No, no, no. He didn't play any music? No, no. He was just a common laborer. One other question, and then I'll stop, is about the Creole people here. Did they speak the Creole dialect or any language, you know, like French?
